name: ChEETAh
question: Does routine change of sterile gloves and instruments before abdominal wound closure reduce 30-day surgical site infection?

design.blinding: unmasked surgical teams and outcome assessors; patients masked

arms.label: Routine change of sterile gloves and instruments before wound closure

design.population: Adults and children having emergency or elective clean-contaminated, contaminated or dirty abdominal surgery through an incision of at least 5 cm, excluding cesarean section, in 81 hospitals in seven low- and middle-income countries.
design.description: Pragmatic multicenter cluster-randomized superiority trial, hospitals randomized
design.locator: Lancet full text: Methods, Results, Figure 1

verdictNote: Adjusted RR 0.87 for 30-day SSI; the design targeted a 4-point absolute reduction.
takeaway: ChEETAh randomized 81 hospitals in seven low- and middle-income countries to routine glove and instrument change before abdominal wound closure versus current practice; 30-day surgical site infection was 16.1% versus 18.9% (adjusted risk ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.79–0.95).

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: NIHR Global Research Health Unit on Global Surgery. Routine sterile glove and instrument change at the time of abdominal wound closure to prevent surgical site infection (ChEETAh): a pragmatic, cluster-randomised trial in seven low-income and middle-income countries. *Lancet.* 2022;400(10365):1767-1776. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(22)01884-0
reports.followUp: 30 days after surgery; primary outcome analyzed in 12,557 of 13,301 patients

results.measure: SSI within 30 days (superficial or deep incisional, CDC criteria); adjusted risk ratio
results.note: Modified intention-to-treat population (patients lost to follow-up, refusing consent or dying before assessment excluded). The abstract prints 16.0% for the intervention group; the Results text and Figure 3 print 16.1%. Multilevel log-binomial model adjusted for hospital type, contamination, operative approach and timing of surgery. The sample size assumed a 16% control rate and a 4-point absolute (25% relative) reduction, the minimum clinically important difference chosen by an international surgeon group.

results.note: Modified Poisson model because the log-binomial model did not converge.

results.measure: Self-reported return to normal activities by 30 days; adjusted risk ratio
results.note: Modified Poisson model because the log-binomial model did not converge.
Geometric mean ratio 1.12 (95% CI 0.97–1.25; P = 0.083) on log-transformed stay, measured to the nearest whole day.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: The authors did not anticipate or collect specific data on serious adverse events.

harms.label: Mortality within 30 days
harms.note: Adjusted risk ratio 0.88 (95% CI 0.70–1.10; P = 0.26). Deaths before outcome assessment excluded from the primary analysis: 313 and 309.

harms.label: Unexpected readmission for a wound-related problem
Unexpected reoperation for a wound-related problem
harms.note: Table 3 prints 2.3% for the current-practice group (157/6,674 is 2.35%). Adjusted risk ratio 0.73 (95% CI 0.48–1.10; P = 0.14).

delivery.label: Intervention
delivery.value: Operating surgeons, assistants and scrub staff changed sterile gloves (outer gloves if double gloved) and used a separate sterile needle holder, forceps and scissors for abdominal wall closure, after the abdominal part of the operation and before handling the wound edges.

delivery.label: Planned and achieved sample
delivery.value: Planned: 90% power to detect a fall in SSI from 16% to 12%, requiring 12,800 participants from at least 64 clusters. Achieved: 13,301 patients from 81 hospitals, recruited 24 June 2020 to 31 March 2022.
delivery.locator: Lancet full text: abstract; Methods (Statistical analysis); Results

delivery.label: Both components changed in intervention; at least one component changed in control
delivery.note: The Results print 98.3% for the intervention group (6,044/6,144 is 98.37%). Among 5,789 intervention patients analyzed for the primary outcome, 100 did not receive the change; in the control group 45 had a glove change only, 3 an instrument change only and 10 both.

delivery.label: Hospitals randomized and analyzed
delivery.note: One control hospital withdrew after randomization and enrolled no patients. 65/81 hospitals (80%) were referral centers, with 20 to 3,400 beds. Median 200 patients per hospital (IQR 91–220).

delivery.label: Patients excluded from the primary analysis
delivery.note: Intervention group: 11 refused consent, 26 lost to follow-up, 313 died before outcome assessment, 5 missing. Control group: 24, 53, 309 and 3.

delivery.label: Age group
delivery.locator: Lancet full text: abstract; Results; Table 1

delivery.label: Emergency surgery
delivery.note: Elective surgery 6,125/13,301 (46.0%) overall. The primary model adjusted for timing of surgery.

delivery.label: Urologic operations
delivery.note: 679 urologic operations in total. Gynecologic operations 1,204 (19.6%) versus 1,870 (26.1%); colon and rectum 840 (13.7%) versus 644 (9.0%).

delivery.label: Prophylactic antibiotic within 60 minutes before incision
Outcome assessment by telephone

delivery.label: Glove supply
delivery.value: Mölnlycke Healthcare provided sterile BioGel gloves to intervention-group hospitals as an unrestricted donation.

results.note: With Mexico unit costs the cost difference was $0.15 (95% CI −1.78 to 2.18) and with Ghana unit costs −$1.79 (95% CI −8.82 to −0.48); the authors report cost-effectiveness in all three.
